standard.title: Specification for Sheepsfoot Roller (शेप्सफुट रोलर — विशिष्टि)
standard.sector: Mechanical Engineering / Construction Plant and Machinery

sectional_committee.name: Construction Plant and Machinery Sectional Committee

standard.description: This Indian Standard prescribes the sizes, classification, material specifications, design configurations, machine characteristics, and performance/finishing requirements for transportable sheepsfoot rollers (both single-drum and double-drum models) used for the solid compaction of earth embankments, subgrade soils, subgrade road localized breakups, highway fills, dam approaches, and airports.
standard.scope: This Indian Standard prescribes the sizes, classification, material specifications, design configurations, machine characteristics, and performance/finishing requirements for transportable sheepsfoot rollers (both single-drum and double-drum models) used for the solid compaction of earth embankments, subgrade soils, subgrade road localized breakups, highway fills, dam approaches, and airports.

supersedes: None (First national standard formulated to establish uniform
and safety guidelines for sheepsfoot compaction rollers in the Indian construction sector)

certification.description: Voluntary Product Specification. Manufacturers are highly encouraged to obtain a valid BIS license to stamp or attach the physical ISI 'Standard Mark' directly on the main frame or nameplate of the compaction roller to certify construction and performance conformity.
requirements: Observed or calculated final test values, observed dimensions, or physical properties must be rounded off mathematically in accordance with IS 2:1960. The number of significant places retained should match that of the specified value in the standard.

Standard sheepsfoot rollers must feature drums with standardized outer diameters (less tamping feet) to ensure correct ground impact loading: (a) Single-drum models = 1000 or 1060 mm; (b) Two-drum in-line models = 1000, 1060, or 1520 mm.
Rollers are classified based on standard tamping feet geometries to accommodate different soil characteristics: Sheepsfoot, club foot, cone foot, pyramid foot, or cylinder foot.

Key operational design limits are specified and must be reported: overall length (including drawbar), overall width, drum length, drum shell diameter, number of tamping feet, tamping area (footprint), tamping foot length, and total empty and ballasted weight.
Rivet holes must be drilled or reamed. Rivet heads must be full, neatly made, concentric with the rivet holes, and in full contact with the surface of the member.

Joint surfaces must be clean of paint, rust, scale, and grease. Welds must transmit design stresses smoothly without showing permanent deformation or joint failure when the parts connected are subjected to proof and service loads.
Painted parts of the roller must be thoroughly cleaned, treated, and painted with anti-corrosive primer and synthetic machinery enamel paint in accordance with relevant Indian Standards.
